Master Examination Study Guide: Special Moral Theology (9H23)

Section I: Moral Theology of Life (Morale della Vita)

Pontificia Università della Santa Croce (PUSC) • Ciclo I (STB Anno III, Semestre I)

Professor: Rev. Prof. Pablo Requena, MD, STD

Examination Date: Written Partial (Tuesday, 24 November 2026 / February Session)

---

Guide Architecture & Roadmap

This master document serves as the cumulative study dossier for the written examination (accounting for 80% of the grade of Section I). It is designed to be modular so that further Magisterial documents and lecture themes can be incorporated over the coming days:

  • Module I: Instruction Donum vitae (CDF, 22 February 1987) (Current Module)
  • Module II: Instruction Dignitas personae (CDF, 8 September 2008) (Current Module)
  • Module III: Encyclical Evangelium vitae (John Paul II, 25 March 1995) (To be expanded)
  • Module IV: End-of-Life, Euthanasia & Proportionality (Iura et bona 1980, Samaritanus bonus 2020) (To be expanded)
  • Module V: Magisterial Addresses & CDF Responsa (Pius XII, John Paul II, CDF 2007) (To be expanded)
  • Module VI: Examination Blueprints, Question Bank & Model Answers (To be expanded)

    • ---

    Examination Structure & Grading Rules

    Prof. Pablo Requena structures the written examination into three distinct parts:

    1. Part 1: 20 Multiple-Choice Questions (Scelta Multipla)

  • Assesses direct comprehension and textual retention of the official Magisterial documents.
  • Requires precise familiarity with paragraph numbers, technical definitions, and ethical distinctions.

    • 2. Part 2: 4 Short-Answer Questions (Domande Brevi)

  • Requires concise, conceptually exact theological formulations (approx. 3–5 lines each).
  • Includes specific biblical loci (e.g. Genesis 9:6), encyclical sections (e.g. EV 99), and secular bioethical citations (e.g. Ruth Macklin in BMJ 2003).
  • The "1 or 0" Rule: For verbatim Magisterial definitions (such as direct abortion in EV 58 or euthanasia in Iura et bona II), full credit is awarded only for the precise, textual definition; inexact or descriptive approximations receive zero.

    • 3. Part 3: 1 Synthetic Essay Question (Domanda da Rispondere in una Pagina)

  • A single-page development testing speculative synthesis, theological argumentation, and personalist criteria (e.g. moral evaluation of assisted reproductive technologies, or ethico-political debates on euthanasia).

    MODULE I: Instruction Donum Vitae (CDF, 22 February 1987)

    Instruction on Respect for Human Life in Its Origin and on the Dignity of Procreation: Replies to Certain Questions of the Day

    Primary Source File: [`sources/magisterium/1987-donum-vitae.md`](file:///C:/Users/antst/Documents/20.%20STB/Year%203/Semester%20I/Morale%20Speciale/sources/magisterium/1987-donum-vitae.md)

    ---

    1. Theological & Anthropological Framework

    Published under the prefecture of Cardinal Joseph Ratzinger, Donum vitae addresses the ethical challenges precipitated by the emergence of In Vitro Fertilisation (IVF / FIVET, inaugurated with Louise Brown in 1978). The document is founded on two core pillars:

    1. The Inviolability of Innocent Human Life: Human life is a gift of God (donum vitae) over which man has stewardship, not absolute dominion.

    2. The Truth of Conjugal Love: Human procreation must be the bodily, personal fruit of the specific conjugal act of reciprocal spousal self-donation.

    ---

    2. Verbatim Formulations to Learn by Heart

    A. Moral Status of the Human Embryo (Donum vitae, I.1)

    Italian:
    "L'essere umano va rispettato e trattato come una persona fin dal suo concepimento e, perciò, da quello stesso momento gli si devono riconoscere i diritti della persona, tra i quali anzitutto il diritto inviolabile di ogni essere umano innocente alla vita."

    >

    English:
    "The human being must be respected and treated as a person from conception, and therefore from that same moment his rights as a person must be recognised, among which in the first place is the inviolable right of every innocent human being to life."
  • Theological & Metaphysical Nuance: Notice the precise formula: "respect treated as a person". The Church does not enter into a philosophical definition of the exact temporal instant of animated ensoulment (animatio), but establishes an unconditional moral obligation: because modern biological science demonstrates that from the formation of the zygote a new, genetically distinct human individual is present with coordinated, autonomous development, the embryo must be accorded the full moral status and inviolable rights of a human person.

    • B. The Decisive Moral Criterion: Assistance vs Substitution (Donum vitae, II.B.7)

    Latin:
    "Si autem medium adhibitum subroget actum coniugalem, hoc medium moraliter non licitum est. Si contra medium adhibitum actum coniugalem adiuvet... moraliter licitum est."

    >

    Italian:
    "Se il mezzo tecnico facilita l'atto coniugale o lo aiuta a raggiungere i suoi obiettivi naturali, può essere moralmente accettato; se invece la procedura si sostituisce all'atto coniugale, essa è moralmente illecita."

    >

    English:
    "If the technical means facilitates the conjugal act or helps it to achieve its natural ends, it can be morally accepted; but if the procedure substitutes for the conjugal act, it is morally illicit."
  • The Adiuvet vs Subroget Distinction:
  • Licit Assistance (Adiuvet): Medical interventions that assist, accompany, or cure pathology in order to enable marital intercourse to attain fertilisation (e.g. hormonal therapy, surgical tubal clearance, NaProTechnology). The spouses remain the true personal and physical cause of procreation.
  • Illicit Substitution (Subroget): Medical procedures that replace the marital act (e.g. IVF/FIVET, ICSI, artificial insemination via masturbation). Procreation is transferred to the laboratory, subjecting the conceived child to technological domination (dominium technicum).

    • C. Inseparable Connection of Unitive and Procreative Meanings (Donum vitae, II.B.4)

    Building directly upon Paul VI's Humanae vitae (n. 12), the document affirms the nexus inseparabilis: the conjugal act possesses two intrinsic, divinely instituted meanings: the unitive meaning (significatio unitiva) and the procreative meaning (significatio procreativa). Just as contraception severs the procreative meaning from the unitive act, so artificial reproduction severs the unitive act from procreation. Both separations offend the truth of human love.

    ---

    3. Comprehensive Breakdown by Parts & Questions

    Part I: Respect for Human Embryos

    1. Prenatal Diagnosis (Diagnosi Prenatale, I.2):

  • Licit: If it respects the life and integrity of the embryo and fetus, is directed toward his individual healing, and provides informed consent to the parents.
  • Illicit: If it is undertaken with the intention of procuring an abortion should a defect or disease be detected (eugenic mentality), or if it utilises diagnostic methods that pose disproportionate risks to the unborn child. A woman who requests diagnosis with the intention of aborting commits a grave sin; any physician who encourages this is an accomplice.

    • 2. Therapeutic Interventions on Embryos (I.3):

  • Licit: Only if they respect the life and integrity of the individual embryo, do not subject him to disproportionate risks, and are aimed directly at his healing, improvement of health, or individual survival.

    • 3. Research & Experimentation on Embryos (I.4):

  • Illicit: Treating human embryos as mere experimental biological material or clinical disposable objects is a crime against their dignity.
  • Experimentation is licit only when there is moral certainty that it will not harm the child or the mother, and free parental consent has been given. Non-therapeutic research that risks the life or integrity of the embryo is intrinsically immoral.

    • 4. Use of Embryos Obtained In Vitro for Research (I.5):

  • Producing human embryos in vitro for research or commercial purposes is gravely immoral.
  • Procuring or manipulating "surplus" embryos generated through IVF constitutes grave instrumentalisation.

    • 5. Manipulation, Freezing, and Hybrids (I.6):

  • Any attempt to produce human-animal chimeras, hybridisation, ectogenesis (artificial gestation outside the uterus), or twin-fission cloning is intrinsically evil and violates human dignity.

    • ---

    Part II: Interventions upon Human Procreation

    ##### A. Heterologous Artificial Fertilisation (Donor Gametes / Surrogacy)

  • Moral Evaluation: Gravely illicit (actus intrinsece malus).
  • Four Doctrinal Rationale Points:

    • 1. Violation of the Unity of Marriage: Marriage confers upon spouses the exclusive right to become father and mother only through each other. Introducing third-party gametes (sperm donor or egg donor) violates marital fidelity.

    2. Harm to the Child: Denies the child his fundamental right to know his biological lineage, origin, and genealogy, creating a split between genetic, gestational, and social parentage.

    3. Rupture of the Spousal Covenant: Subverts family unity and introduces ontological alien elements into the spousal covenant.

    4. Surrogate Motherhood (Maternità surrogata, II.A.3): Intrinsically illicit. It treats the woman's body and maternal gestation as a commercial commodity, alienates the mother from her conceived child, and deprives the child of his right to be carried and nurtured by his mother.

    ##### B. Homologous Artificial Fertilisation (Husband and Wife)

  • Moral Evaluation of Homologous IVF (FIVET): Gravely illicit (actus intrinsece malus).
  • Core Theological Arguments:

    • 1. Depersonalisation of Generation: Replaces the personal self-gift of spousal intercourse with a mechanical laboratory procedure performed by biological technicians. The child is treated as a manufactured object (productum technologicum) under laboratory control (dominium technicum), rather than as a gift of personal love (filius ut donum).

    2. Inherent Destruction of Embryos (Perdita embrionaria): In vitro fertilisation routinely requires hyperovulation, the creation of supernumerary embryos, selective discard, and cryopreservation, thereby causing a mass loss of human lives.

    3. Severing the Nexus Inseparabilis: Procreation is achieved outside the marital act, breaking the sacred bond between love and life established by God.

  • Homologous Artificial Insemination (AIH, II.B.6):
  • Illicit: If the sperm is obtained via masturbation and substitutes for marital intercourse.
  • Licit: If the technical device assists an already completed conjugal act (e.g. using a perforated non-spermicidal sheath to collect semen during natural marital intercourse and assisting its transit).

    • ##### C. Pastoral Response to Infertility (II.B.8)

  • Infertility is a heavy cross, but marriage does not confer a "right to have a child" (non datur ius ad prolem).
  • A child is not a piece of property or a commodity to which spouses have an entitlement; a child is a person, a transcendent gift.
  • Christian spouses facing infertility are called to authentic spiritual fruitfulness, foster care, legitimate adoption, educational initiatives, and works of charity.

    • ---

    MODULE II: Instruction Dignitas Personae (CDF, 8 September 2008)

    Instruction on Certain Bioethical Questions

    Primary Source File: [`sources/magisterium/2008-dignitas-personae.md`](file:///C:/Users/antst/Documents/20.%20STB/Year%203/Semester%20I/Morale%20Speciale/sources/magisterium/2008-dignitas-personae.md)

    ---

    1. Continuity & Developments from Donum Vitae

    Published twenty-one years after Donum vitae under Pope Benedict XVI and Cardinal William Levada, Dignitas personae updates Catholic bioethics in response to new biomedical advances: Intracytoplasmic Sperm Injection (ICSI), embryo cryopreservation, Pre-implantation Genetic Diagnosis (PGD), interceptive contraception, embryonic stem cell research, somatic versus germ-line gene therapy, cloning, and fetal cell lines.

    ---

    2. Verbatim Formulations to Learn by Heart

    A. The Three Fundamental Goods (Dignitas personae, n. 12)

    Italian:
    "Nel valutare la portata morale dei recenti sviluppi delle scienze mediche... le nuove tecniche mediche devono rispettare tre beni fondamentali:
    a) il diritto alla vita e all'integrità fisica di ogni essere umano dal concepimento fino alla morte naturale;
    b) l'unità del matrimonio, che comporta il reciproco rispetto del diritto dei coniugi a diventare padre e madre soltanto l'uno attraverso l'altro;
    c) i valori specificamente umani della sessualità, che esigono che la procreazione debba essere perseguita come il frutto dell'atto coniugale specifico dell'amore tra gli sposi."

    >

    English:
    "In evaluating the moral dimension of recent developments in medical sciences... new medical techniques must respect three fundamental goods:
    a) The right to life and physical integrity of every human being from conception to natural death;
    b) The unity of marriage, which entails reciprocal respect for the right within marriage to become a father or mother only together with the other spouse;
    c) The specifically human values of sexuality, which require that procreation be pursued as the fruit of the specific conjugal act of mutual spousal love."

    B. Moral Evaluation of Embryo Cryopreservation (Dignitas personae, nn. 18–19)

    Italian:
    "La crioconservazione è incompatibile con il rispetto dovuto agli embrioni umani: essa presuppone la loro produzione in vitro; li espone a gravi rischi di morte o di danno per la loro integrità fisica... li priva almeno temporaneamente dell'accoglienza e della gestazione materna; li pone in una situazione suscettibile di ulteriori offese e manipolazioni... Tutto ciò comporta che le migliaia di embrioni abbandonati determinano una situazione di ingiustizia di fatto insanabile."

    >

    English:
    "Cryopreservation is incompatible with the respect owed to human embryos: it presupposes their in vitro production; exposes them to grave risks of death or harm to physical integrity... deprives them at least temporarily of maternal reception and gestation; and places them in a situation susceptible to further offenses and manipulations... All this leads to the conclusion that the thousands of abandoned embryos represent an unjust situation which in fact cannot be resolved (situazione di ingiustizia di fatto insanabile)."

    C. Pre-implantation Genetic Diagnosis: PGD / DGP (Dignitas personae, n. 22)

    Italian:
    "La diagnosi pre-impianto è un'espressione della mentalità eugenetica che accetta l'aborto selettivo per impedire la nascita di bambini affetti da varie patologie... Tratta l'embrione umano come un semplice materiale di laboratorio."

    >

    English:
    "Pre-implantation genetic diagnosis is an expression of that eugenic mentality which accepts selective abortion in order to prevent the birth of children affected by various anomalies... It treats the human embryo as simple laboratory material."

    D. Interception and Contragestion (Dignitas personae, n. 23)

    Technical Distinction:
    - Interceptive Methods (Intercettivi): Interventions designed to prevent implantation of an already conceived blastocyst (e.g. morning-after pill, NorLevo, ellaOne, Intrauterine Device / IUD).
    - Contragestive Methods (Contragestivi): Interventions that provoke the detachment or expulsion of an already implanted embryo (e.g. RU-486 / mifepristone).
    - Magisterial Verdict: Anyone who seeks to prevent implantation or provoke expulsion directly wills abortion ("chi desidera impedire l'annidamento di un embrione già concepito... persegue di fatto un aborto").

    E. Biological Material of Illicit Origin & Refusal of Independence (Dignitas personae, nn. 34–35)

    Rejection of the "Criterion of Independence":
    "In questo senso, non è sufficiente il criterio di indipendenza formulato da alcuni comitati etici, secondo cui l'uso di materiale biologico di origine illecita sarebbe eticamente ammissibile purché vi sia una netta separazione tra coloro che producono, congelano o uccidono gli embrioni e i ricercatori che sviluppano la sperimentazione scientifica."

    >

    - The Church explicitly rejects the secular ethical theory that researchers are morally clean simply because they did not perform the original abortion or embryonic destruction themselves.
    - Using such biological material contributes to creating commercial demand and cultural acceptance for illicit practices (cooperatio materialis passiva mediata that risks grave scandal).

    ---

    3. Exhaustive Thematic Breakdown across All 37 Numbers

    First Part: Anthropological, Theological & Ethical Foundations (nn. 1–10)

  • n. 1: To every human being, from conception to natural death, is due the dignity of a person.
  • nn. 4–5: Modern genetics confirms that fertilisation initiates a new biological individual with autonomous epigenetic development. The zygote contains the full genetic programme; no subsequent milestone introduces an ontological qualitative leap.
  • nn. 6–7: Rejection of philosophical theories of gradual personhood (which condition personal dignity on brain activity, consciousness, or relational capacities).
  • n. 8: The human embryo is from the outset a subject of personal dignity (subiectum iuris), not an object of property or scientific manipulation.

    • Second Part: New Problems Concerning Procreation (nn. 11–23)

  • n. 14: IVF intrinsically results in embryonic mortality: a tiny percentage of created embryos actually achieve live birth, while the vast majority are frozen, destroyed, or discarded.
  • n. 17: Intracytoplasmic Sperm Injection (ICSI): Illicit for the same reasons as IVF, with additional physical risks: bypasses natural biological selection, resulting in higher chromosomal anomalies.
  • n. 19: The Question of "Prenatal Adoption" of Abandoned Frozen Embryos:
  • Evaluates proposals to allow infertile couples to thaw and gestate "orphan" frozen embryos (adozione prenatale).
  • While praising the subjective intention of saving innocent human lives, the Instruction concludes that this proposal presents insurmountable moral and legal problems: it legitimates the technological reproductive market, instrumentalises gestation, and violates the unitive truth of marriage.
  • Hence, the situation of cryopreserved embryos is an irremediable injustice (situazione di ingiustizia di fatto insanabile): no morally licit solution exists to resolve their condition once frozen.
  • n. 20: Freezing of Oocytes (Congelamento degli ovociti):
  • While less gravely disordered than embryo freezing (since an oocyte is not a human individual), oocyte freezing undertaken in the context of IVF remains morally illicit because it belongs to an intrinsically evil reproductive chain.
  • n. 21: Embryo Reduction (Riduzione embrionaria):
  • In multiple IVF pregnancies, doctors frequently perform "selective reduction" (injecting potassium chloride directly into embryonic hearts). This is direct, intentional abortion (homicidium).

    • Third Part: Gene Therapy, Cloning, Stem Cells & Illicit Material (nn. 24–37)

    ##### 1. Gene Therapy (nn. 25–27)

  • Somatic Gene Therapy (Terapia genica somatica, n. 26):
  • Morally Licit: Directed at treating genetic pathology in non-reproductive somatic cells (e.g. bone marrow, lungs), provided there are proportionate clinical benefits and acceptable risks.
  • Germ-Line Gene Therapy (Terapia genica germinale, n. 27):
  • Morally Illicit in Current State: Modifies genetic traits transmitted to future generations. Carries grave, unpredictable risks of transmission of genetic damage, requires in vitro fertilisation, and opens the door to eugenic manipulation ("enhancing" human performance, creating genetically superior classes).

    • ##### 2. Human Cloning (nn. 28–30)

  • Reproductive Cloning (Clonazione riproduttiva): Gravely immoral; creates a genetic copy of a single parent without sexual reproduction, imposing pre-determined identity and treating the clone as an biological copy.
  • Therapeutic Cloning (Clonazione terapeutica): Even more perverse; creates human embryos through somatic cell nuclear transfer (SCNT) with the explicit intention of harvesting their stem cells at the blastocyst stage and destroying them.

    • ##### 3. Stem Cells: Adult vs Embryonic (nn. 31–32)

  • Adult Stem Cells & Induced Pluripotent Stem Cells (iPSC):
  • Morally Licit: Sourced from adult bone marrow, umbilical cord blood, fat tissue, or reprogrammed somatic cells. Does not destroy human life and demonstrates superior therapeutic success.
  • Human Embryonic Stem Cells (hESC):
  • Morally Illicit: Intrinsically evil because the procurement of embryonic stem cells requires the deliberate physical destruction of the human blastocyst.

    • ##### 4. Use of Biological Material of Illicit Origin (nn. 34–35)

  • Covers the use of historic fetal cell lines (e.g. WI-38, MRC-5, HEK-293) derived from elective abortions:

    • 1. Catholic researchers and health institutions have a moral duty to demand alternatives and bear witness to the value of human life.

    2. If no alternatives exist, grave health threats (e.g. rubella, lethal pandemics) can permit the temporary use of vaccines with remote, passive material cooperation, provided there is active objection to the underlying evil and no scandal is given.

    MODULE IV: End-of-Life Ethics, Euthanasia & Proportionality

    Authoritative Guide to Iura et bona (1980), Samaritanus bonus (2020), and CDF Responsa on ANH (2007)

    Primary Sources:

  • [`sources/magisterium/1980-iura-et-bona.md`](file:///C:/Users/antst/Documents/20.%20STB/Year%203/Semester%20I/Morale%20Speciale/sources/magisterium/1980-iura-et-bona.md)
  • [`sources/magisterium/2020-samaritanus-bonus.md`](file:///C:/Users/antst/Documents/20.%20STB/Year%203/Semester%20I/Morale%20Speciale/sources/magisterium/2020-samaritanus-bonus.md)
  • [`sources/magisterium/2007-cdf-responsum-anh.md`](file:///C:/Users/antst/Documents/20.%20STB/Year%203/Semester%20I/Morale%20Speciale/sources/magisterium/2007-cdf-responsum-anh.md)

    • ---

    1. Declaration on Euthanasia: Iura et Bona (CDF, 5 May 1980)

    A. Verbatim Definition of Euthanasia in the Strict Sense (Section II)

    Italian (Mandatory Exam Formulation):
    "Per eutanasia in senso vero e proprio si deve intendere un'azione o un'omissione che di sua natura e nelle intenzioni procura la morte, allo scopo di eliminare ogni dolore."

    >

    English:
    "By euthanasia in the proper sense is understood an action or an omission which of itself or by intention causes death, in order that all suffering may in this way be eliminated."
  • The Three Essential Elements (The "1 or 0" Scoring Standard):

    • 1. Act of Commission or Omission: Can be committed positively by administering a lethal substance (actio), or negatively by omitting basic ordinary care (omissio).

    2. Intrinsic Object or Intention: The death is either the intrinsic nature of the act itself (finis operis / de sua natura), or the formal intention of the acting subject (finis operantis / in intentione).

    3. Motive: The subjective motive of eliminating suffering (allo scopo di eliminare ogni dolore). Even noble subjective motives (compassion, relief of misery) do not alter the objective species of homicide.

  • Moral Evaluation: Gravely illicit (actus intrinsece malus), a direct violation of the divine law and a crime against innocent human life.

    • B. The Use of Painkillers and Analgesics (Section III)

  • Principle of Double Effect (Praeter Intentionem):

    • It is morally licit to administer narcotics and analgesics to alleviate intractable pain, even if they foreseeably shorten the patient's life, provided:

    1. Death is not willed either as an end or as a chosen means;

    2. There is no other clinical means to alleviate the pain;

    3. The intention is strictly to suppress pain, with death being merely an unintended, tolerated side-effect (praeter intentionem).

  • The Duty to Preserve Consciousness:

    • The dying person must not be deprived of consciousness without a grave clinical reason, because consciousness is necessary to satisfy moral and familial duties, settle temporal affairs, and prepare spiritually to meet God through the Sacraments.

    C. Due Proportion in the Use of Remedies: Beyond Ordinary vs Extraordinary (Section IV)

  • Iura et bona introduced a decisive conceptual shift: while preserving the classic casuistic distinction between ordinary and extraordinary means, it introduced the modern, clinical category of proportionate versus disproportionate means (mezzi proporzionati vs sproporzionati).
  • Refusal of Therapeutic Obstinacy (Accanimento Terapeutico):

    • When death is imminent and inevitable, it is morally licit in conscience to refuse or discontinue medical procedures that would only procure a precarious, painful, or burdensome prolongation of life, provided that the normal care due to the sick person (hygiene, hydration, pain management) is never interrupted.

    ---

    2. Letter Samaritanus Bonus (CDF, 14 July 2020)

    Published by the Congregation for the Doctrine of the Faith under Pope Francis, Samaritanus bonus addresses the modern clinical and legislative landscape: legalized assisted suicide, deep continuous palliative sedation, artificial nutrition in vegetative states, and sacramental pastoral care.

    Key Tested Paragraphs in Part V (Magisterial Teaching):

    1. V.1 Prohibition of Euthanasia and Assisted Suicide:

  • Defines euthanasia as a crimen contra vitam humanam and an actus intrinsece malus, which no authority, law, or personal intention can ever legitimise.
  • Clarifies that assisted suicide (suicidio medicalmente assistito) incurs the same objective gravity, aggravating the moral disorder by drawing medical professionals into formal complicity with suicide.

    • 2. V.2 The Moral Obligation to Avoid Therapeutic Obstinacy (Accanimento Terapeutico):

  • Catholic ethics strictly distinguishes euthanasia from the licit withdrawal of futile, aggressive treatments (ostinazione irragionevole). Withdrawing treatments that have become disproportionate or physiologically ineffective is not causing death; it is accepting the human condition and allowing natural death to take its course.

    • 3. V.3 & V.8 Artificial Nutrition and Hydration (ANH): The Three Legitimate Limits:

  • General Rule: The administration of water and food (even artificially via nasogastric tube or PEG) represents basic ordinary care due to the patient (cura ordinaria dovuta al malato), not a medical treatment. It is morally obligatory so long as it preserves life and prevents the agonizing death of dehydration and starvation.
  • The Three Strict Clinical Conditions Permitting Withdrawal of ANH:

    • 1. Physiological Futility / Inability to Assimilate: The patient's body can no longer absorb or digest nutrients (e.g. advanced intestinal necrosis, end-stage bowel ischaemia, irreversible multiorgan failure).

    2. Disproportionate Physical Burden / Severe Harm: The administration causes acute physical suffering or life-threatening complications (e.g. repeated pulmonary aspiration pneumonia, severe painful esophageal reflux, severe persistent site infection).

    3. Terminal Agonal Phase: In the imminent hours of active dying, physiological dehydration is part of the natural dying process; forcing hydration can cause fluid overload, peripheral oedema, and distressing pulmonary secretions (death rattle).

  • Crucial Negative Criterion: ANH can never be discontinued on the grounds of cognitive loss, persistent unconsciousness, or intellectual impairment (Persistent Vegetative State / PVS). Discontinuing food and water in such patients constitutes intentional euthanasia by omission.

    • 4. V.4 & V.7 Palliative Care and Deep Continuous Sedation (Sedazione Palliativa Profonda):

  • Definition: The controlled administration of sedatives to induce unconsciousness until natural death, aimed at managing intolerable, untreatable symptoms in the terminal stage.
  • The Three Criteria of Moral Licitness:

    • 1. Refractory Symptoms: Applicable strictly in the imminent terminal phase for refractory symptoms (physical pain or psychological anguish that has proven unresponsive to all available palliative protocols).

    2. Principle of Double Effect: The intention must be solely to relieve suffering (sedare dolorem); death must neither be intended as an end nor chosen as a means (praeter intentionem).

    3. Sacramental and Spiritual Preparation: The patient must have the conscious opportunity to settle familial duties and receive the Sacraments (Penance, Anointing of the Sick, and Viaticum) before consciousness is permanently relinquished.

  • Requena's Pastoral & Clinical Alert: Prof. Requena cautions against covert hospital practices where deep sedation is initiated precipitously without refractory pain and fluids are simultaneously discontinued, effectively inducing dehydration-death within 4 to 5 days under the benign label of palliation.

    • 5. V.9 Conscientious Objection:

  • Catholic healthcare professionals and Catholic healthcare institutions have an absolute, non-negotiable moral duty of conscientious objection against euthanasia, assisted suicide, and abortion.
  • Catholic hospitals are strictly forbidden from participating in institutional schemes or hosting procedures directed toward assisted dying.

    • 6. V.Il Sacramental Discernment for Those Requesting Euthanasia:

  • Sacramental Refusal: Those who formally request assisted suicide or euthanasia cannot receive the Sacraments of Penance, Anointing of the Sick, or Viaticum so long as they obstinately maintain their intention.
  • Theological Reason: Sacramental absolution requires sincere contrition and the firm purpose of amendment (propositum emendationis), which necessarily entails the explicit revocation of the homicidal request. Administering sacraments to someone obstinate in euthanasia constitutes a grave public scandal and a sacrilegious simulation of the sacrament.

    • ---

    3. CDF Responses on Artificial Nutrition and Hydration (1 August 2007)

    Promulgated under Pope Benedict XVI and Cardinal William Levada following international legal controversies (e.g. Terri Schiavo and Eluana Englaro), this document provides authoritative, definitive judgements on the vegetative state:

    The First Responsum: Moral Obligation

  • Question: Is the administration of food and water (whether by natural or artificial means) to a patient in a "vegetative state" morally obligatory, except when they cannot be assimilated by the patient's body or cannot be administered without causing significant physical discomfort?
  • Authoritative Response: AFFIRMATIVE (Yes).
  • Doctrinal Rationale: The administration of water and food, even by artificial means, is in principle an ordinary and proportionate means of preserving life. It accomplishes its proper natural end: the nourishment and hydration of the human subject, preventing death by starvation and dehydration.

    • The Second Responsum: Permanent Vegetative State

  • Question: When nutrition and hydration are being supplied by artificial means to a patient in a "permanent vegetative state", may they be discontinued when competent physicians judge with moral certainty that the patient will never recover consciousness?
  • Authoritative Response: NEGATIVE (No).
  • Doctrinal Rationale: A patient in a permanent vegetative state is an individual human person with fundamental personal dignity. Personal dignity is ontological and inalienable; it does not disappear with the loss of higher cognitive functions or relational consciousness. Withdrawing ANH in this condition is directly causing death by starvation, which constitutes euthanasia by omission.

    • ---

    4. Historical & Theoretical Synthesis of Medical Means

    A. Francisco de Vitoria, O.P. (1483–1546, Relectio de Homicidio)

  • Foundational Dominican theologian of the School of Salamanca who established the scholastic framework of medical preservation of life:
  • Media Communia: Ordinary food and remedies that are accessible and proportionate; their use is obligatory under natural law.
  • Media Difficilia: Burdensome or extraordinary measures; not obligatory.
  • The Principle of Quaedam Impossibilitas: Vitoria taught that if taking food causes a dying or severely ill person grave horror, intense nausea, or unbearable pain, they are morally excused from taking it. The moral impossibility excuses from the physical obligation.

    • B. Pope Pius XII (1957 Allocution to Anaesthesiologists)

  • Defined the classical Magisterial boundary regarding resuscitation techniques and mechanical ventilators:
  • Man has a duty to preserve life through ordinary means (mezzi ordinari), but is not bound to use extraordinary means (mezzi straordinari) that impose a crushing burden on the patient or family.
  • When vital organs are kept functioning purely by artificial machines after catastrophic trauma, the physician may licitly withdraw the machines if resuscitation offers no reasonable hope of recovery.
  • Addressed the metaphysical question of the separation of the soul (separatio animae a corpore): it is the duty of biological science to verify the cessation of organismic vital functions, which signals that life has departed.

    • C. Prof. Pablo Requena's 4-Quadrant Matrix of Medical Means (2019)

    Prof. Requena resolves the confusion between "ordinary/extraordinary" and "proportionate/disproportionate" through a rigorous clinical-ethical matrix:

                      ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────┐
                  │          DISPROPORTIONATE MEANS              │
                  │   (Therapeutic Obstinacy / Illicit)          │
▲ UPPER THRESHOLD ├──────────────────────────────────────────────┤ ◄ Ceiling of Futility
│                 │                                              │
│                 │       SPACE OF THERAPEUTIC PRUDENCE          │
│                 │                                              │
│                 │   • Extraordinary & Proportionate (Optional) │
│                 │   • Proportionate Experimental Treatments    │
│                 │                                              │
▼ LOWER THRESHOLD ├──────────────────────────────────────────────┤ ◄ Floor of Abandonment
                  │            ORDINARY MEANS                    │
                  │   (Basic Care & Hydration / Obligatory)      │
                  └──────────────────────────────────────────────┘

    1. Ordinary Means: Always Obligatory (The Lower Threshold; falling below it constitutes therapeutic abandonment / abbandono terapeutico).

    2. Extraordinary Means: Optional (Non-obligatory, but morally licit if the patient chooses to pursue proportionate clinical benefit).

    3. Proportionate Means: Morally Licit (Reasonable proportion between physical/economic burden and expected clinical benefit).

    4. Disproportionate Means: Always Illicit (The Upper Threshold; exceeding it constitutes therapeutic obstinacy / accanimento terapeutico).

  • Between the lower floor and the upper ceiling lies the vast Space of Therapeutic Prudence, where physicians, patients, and families discern specific clinical decisions in conscience.

    • ---

    MODULE V: Quick-Reference Memory Anchors for the Exam

    1. The "1 or 0" Definition of Direct Abortion (Evangelium vitae, n. 58):

  • "L'uccisione deliberata e diretta, comunque venga attuata, di un essere umano nella fase iniziale della sua esistenza, compresa tra il concepimento e la nascita."

    • 2. The "1 or 0" Definition of Euthanasia (Iura et bona, Section II):

  • "Un'azione o un'omissione che di sua natura e nelle intenzioni procura la morte, allo scopo di eliminare ogni dolore."

    • 3. The Three Fundamental Goods (Dignitas personae, n. 12):

  • 1. Right to life and physical integrity from conception to natural death.
  • 2. Unity of marriage (becoming parents only through each other).
  • 3. Specifically human values of sexuality (fruit of conjugal act).

    • 4. The Golden Criterion of Donum vitae (II.B.7):

  • Adiuvet = Licit Assistance to the marital act.
  • Subroget = Illicit Substitution of the marital act by technological dominion.

    • 5. The Three Legitimate Withdrawal Limits of ANH (Samaritanus bonus, V.3):

  • 1. Physiological futility (inability to assimilate food/fluids).
  • 2. Disproportionate physical burden / severe complications.
  • 3. Imminent agonal phase of active dying.

    • 6. The Three Criteria for Deep Continuous Sedation (Samaritanus bonus, V.4):

  • 1. Refractory terminal symptoms only.
  • 2. Double effect (death neither end nor means).
  • 3. Conscious opportunity to settle duties and receive Sacraments prior to sedation.

    • 7. The Status of Frozen Embryos (Dignitas personae, n. 19):

  • "Situazione di ingiustizia di fatto insanabile" (prenatal adoption rejected).

    • 8. PGD Evaluation (Dignitas personae, n. 22):

  • Expression of a eugenic mentality (mentalità eugenetica).

    • 9. The Two CDF 2007 Responsa on ANH:

  • Question 1: AFFIRMATIVE (ANH is ordinary, proportionate, and obligatory).
  • Question 2: NEGATIVE (ANH cannot be withdrawn because consciousness is permanently lost).

    • 10. Refusal of Sacraments in Euthanasia (Samaritanus bonus, V.11):

  • Sacraments cannot be administered so long as the request for euthanasia is obstinately maintained; requires sincere contrition and explicit retraction.

    • Official Examination Blueprint

    Section I: 80% October 2026

    Partial Written Exam

    Covers Moral Theology of Life. Format: 20 Multiple-Choice Questions on Magisterial texts, 4 Short-Answer Questions, and 1 One-Page Synthetic Essay.

    Section I: 20% Due 05 Nov 2026

    Group Case Study

    Max 1,500 words (groups of 4–5). Clinical bioethical case: Heterologous IVF with father-in-law's sperm & donor sperm, 5 cryopreserved embryos, and critical evaluation of AI responses.

    Section II: 100% February 2027

    Final Oral Examination

    *Viva Voce* interrogation on the Special Moral Theology of Fortitude, Temperance, and Chastity (Rodríguez Luño Manual, Chapters 6, 7, and 8).

    🏛️

    The Academic Writing Rubric (PUSC 30 e lode)

    Every top-tier synthetic essay and oral viva defense evaluated at the Pontifical University of the Holy Cross must systematically embody the five classical theological steps:

    1. Status Quaestionis

    Rigorous demarcation of the problem; refutation of false dichotomies and secular anti-language.

    2. Scriptural Roots

    Hebrew and Greek semantic anchors (*Basar, Ruach, Sarx, Zoe*), Decalogue, and *pedagogia divina*.

    3. Patristic Svolta

    Early Church consensus (*Didache*, Tertullian, Augustine) separating medicine from pagan violence.

    4. Metaphysics & Thomas

    Hylomorphism, moral object (*finis operis*), *praeter intentionem*, and rejection of proportionalism.

    5. Magisterial Synthesis

    *GS 22*, the Incarnation, and exact Magisterial loci (*Iura et bona, Donum vitae, EV, SB*).

    Simulated Extended Examination Essays (Interactive Outlines)

    1. Moral Evaluation of Medically Assisted Procreation Techniques ▼ Show Outline & Sources

    Primary Sources: CDF, *Donum vitae* (1987); CDF, *Dignitas personae* (2008); Paul VI, *Humanae vitae* (1968), n. 12; John Paul II, *Evangelium vitae* (1995), n. 14.

    Core Thesis & Argumentative Architecture:

    1. The Inseparable Nexus (*Humanae vitae* 12): The unitive meaning (*significatio unitiva*) and procreative meaning (*significatio procreativa*) cannot be separated without dehumanising generation.
    2. Assistance vs. Substitution (*Donum vitae* II.7): Licit medical assistance aids the marital act (*ut actus coniugalis adiuvetur*); illicit substitution replaces it (*ut actus coniugalis subrogetur*) through laboratory domination.
    3. Heterologous Reproduction: *Actus intrinsece malus*: violates spousal fidelity, the child's right to know genetic origins, and fractures parenthood into six distinct parental figures.
    4. Homologous IVF: *Actus intrinsece malus*: reduces the child from a personal gift (*filius ut donum*) to a commercial/technological product (*productum technologicum*), inherently involving mass embryo loss, cryopreservation, and eugenic screening.
    2. Ethico-Political Arguments For and Against Euthanasia ▼ Show Outline & Sources

    Primary Sources: CDF, *Iura et bona* (1980); CDF, *Samaritanus bonus* (2020); John Paul II, *Evangelium vitae* (1995), nn. 64–74; John Keown, *Euthanasia, Ethics and Public Policy* (Cambridge, 2002).

    Core Thesis & Argumentative Architecture:

    1. Refutation of Secular Arguments: Autonomy is not self-grounding: destroying biological life extinguishes the very substrate of freedom; compassion (*cum-passio*) means sharing pain, not exterminating the sufferer.
    2. The Slippery Slope Doctrine (John Keown): Logical progression from voluntary to non-voluntary euthanasia (e.g. Groningen Protocol for infants); empirical progression in Netherlands, Belgium, Canada dismantling all initial safeguards.
    3. Subtle Social Coercion: The shift from a "right to die" to a perceived "duty to die" among the frail, elderly, and economically insecure.
    4. Destruction of the Fiduciary Medical Bond: Hippocratic deontology is corrupted when doctors are transformed from healers into executioners.
    3. The Ontological, Biological & Moral Status of the Human Embryo ▼ Show Outline & Sources

    Primary Sources: CDF, *Donum vitae* (1987), I.1; CDF, *Dignitas personae* (2008), nn. 4–5; Angelo Rodríguez Luño, *Chosen III*, Chapter 4.

    Core Thesis & Argumentative Architecture:

    1. The Three Biological Criteria: Coordination (epigenetic developmental drive), Continuity (no ontological leaps), and Graduality (continuous differentiation of a single somatic individual).
    2. Refutation of Twinning & Totipotency Objections: Monozygotic twinning does not prove a "pre-embryo"; it simply demonstrates vegetative self-division without compromising individual unity prior to fission.
    3. The *Ratio Personae* Argument: Because human biological life and personal life are indivisible in Aristotelian-Thomistic hylomorphism, the conceived embryo must be respected and treated as a person (*tamquam persona*) with full *ius ad vitam*.
    4. Legitimate Defence, Tyrannicide & Capital Punishment ▼ Show Outline & Sources

    Primary Sources: St. Thomas Aquinas, *Summa Theologiae* II-II, q. 64, a. 7; John Paul II, *Evangelium vitae* (1995), n. 56; Pope Francis, Revision of CCC 2267 (2018).

    Core Thesis & Argumentative Architecture:

    1. The Principle of Double Effect (*Praeter Intentionem*): Moral acts receive species from what is directly intended (*finis operis*); preserving one's life is intended, the aggressor's death is outside intention (*praeter intentionem*).
    2. Tyrannicide (Stauffenberg Plot 1944): Justified under legitimate defense of the community against an active catastrophic aggressor, never under utilitarian consequentialism.
    3. Capital Punishment Development: From retributive justification to strict defensive requirement (EV 56) and modern doctrinal inadmissibility (CCC 2267).

    Rapid-Fire Question Bank (Click to Reveal Answers)

    Q1: How does Iura et bona define euthanasia in the strict sense? 👁️ Reveal
    *"An action or an omission which of itself or by intention causes death, in order that all suffering may in this way be eliminated."* (*Iura et bona*, Section II).
    Q2: What did Ruth Macklin write about human dignity in 2003? 👁️ Reveal
    Macklin published "Dignity is a useless concept" in the *BMJ*, claiming that dignity means nothing more than respect for personal autonomy, collapsing moral worth into actualized conscious capability.
    Q3: What does praeter intentionem mean in legitimate self-defense? 👁️ Reveal
    It means "outside or beside the intention" (St. Thomas Aquinas, ST II-II, q. 64, a. 7). The preservation of one's life is directly willed; the death of the aggressor is unintended (*per accidens*).
    Q4: What are the three Hebrew Old Testament terms for life? 👁️ Reveal
    *Basar* (fragile, mortal flesh), *Chayyim* (fullness/dynamism of life), *Nefesh* (living creature/vital throat seated in blood), and *Ruach* (divine breath/spirit).
    Q5: What are the five Greek New Testament terms for life? 👁️ Reveal
    *Sarx* (mortal flesh), *Soma* (integrated bodily person), *Bios* (temporal duration/livelihood), *Psyche* (earthly soul/vitality), and *Zoe* (divine, eternal, uncreated life).
    Q6: What is the distinction between vita sacra and santità? 👁️ Reveal
    *Vita sacra* is the universal ontological property belonging to every human being from conception to natural death; *Santità* is moral and supernatural conformity to divine grace.
